reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, round-4 fix-verification batch

samples_reviewed.question_text: Make a picture graph to show: cats: 2, dogs: 10, birds: 8, fish: 8. Each 🍎 equals 2.
Make a picture graph to show: apples: 10, bananas: 6, mangoes: 16, grapes: 12. Each 🍎 equals 2.
Make a picture graph to show: roses: 18, sunflowers: 18, tulips: 4, daisies: 6. Each 🍎 equals 2.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: 'Each icon equals 2' with counts to represent is a direct rendering of 'present raw data in a pictograph with a scale' -- I verified every given count (e.g. 18, 16, 12) divides evenly by the stated scale of 2, so no fractional-icon situation is ever presented to the student.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Categories span animals, fruit, flowers, weekdays, and sports across seeds 42-48, and count magnitudes climb into the teens (up to 18), giving reasonable range for a scaled pictograph.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Sentence structure is a short data list plus a one-clause scale statement, appropriate for grade-2 quarter-3 readers who have already met multiplication-adjacent grouping ideas.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Every one of the 7 seeds uses a scale of exactly 2; the competency text says 'pictograph with a scale' generically, and I would expect to see other common scales (5, 10) exercised somewhere in this lc's variant space to build the general skill rather than one fixed multiplier.

competency_alignment.rationale: Content matches the 'present ... in a pictograph with a scale' half of the competency; the reciprocal 'vice versa' (reading a scaled pictograph back to raw/tabular data) is presumably covered by the sibling interpret lc, which is an acceptable division of labor within the node.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Values up to 18 with a scale of 2 (i.e. up to 9 icons) are manageable for a grade-2 student to draw and count, consistent with quarter-3 numeracy expectations.
